Mike L.: ran a perfetto capture on the e2e slow path after the kernel selection change. link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/0a1b2c3d
Jess K.: :eyes: saw a p95 jump in prod last night around 02:14 UTC? p50 stable but tail exploded.
Mike L.: yep — p50 ~45ms, p95 ~410ms on generator workload (seq len median 128, some 1% > 1024)
Olga R.: any obvious span that grew? gateway vs runtime?
Mike L.: perfetto waterfall shows most of the extra time in runtime:kernel_exec for the tails. kernel_select also sometimes takes extra tens of ms when it hits a fallback path.
perfetto-bot: trace uploaded by mike.l@redwood (nsys capture attached). file: /artifacts/nsys/2026-03-15/1934567890.nsys
Sam T.: can you paste the span names/samples? small snippets ok
Mike L.: copy/paste from trace (condensed):
```
client -> gateway:enqueue (2-5ms)
 gateway -> runtime:enqueue (1-4ms)
 runtime:kvcache_lookup (0-1ms)
 runtime:batch_assemble (2-8ms)
 runtime:kernel_select (0.5-50ms)
 runtime:kernel_exec (5-380ms)
 runtime:kvcache_update (1-3ms)
```
Mike L.: note kernel_select sometimes hits the slow path when input tokens > 512 and model heuristics choose a fp16 unoptimized kernel that falls back to a compatible but slower kernel on some GPUs.
Jess K.: do we have correlation with KV cache hits? maybe batching collapsed and prevented reuse of KV prefixes
Olga R.: I checked kv metrics briefly: cache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 60% during that window. batch size distribution also shifted: mean batch size down from 6 to 3 for short bursts.
Sam T.: interesting — so two factors: smaller batches (less amortization) + worse kv hits (more recompute)
Mike L.: I ran an nsys profile of a long tail request. attached timeline snapshot:
```
CUDA kernel timeline:
 - matmul_custom_long (heavy, 310ms)
 - scratch_zeroing (40ms)
 - cuBLAS_sgemm_fallback (50ms)
```
Mike L.: the 'matmul_custom_long' is the kernel we expect for long sequences, but on some steps we see an extra scratch_zeroing call which is the allocator fallback when kernels need extra workspace.
Jess K.: could be memory fragmentation + wrong kernel path chosen that requests larger temporary buffer. kernel selection heuristic probably chose a kernel with lower FLOP efficiency but smaller reported workspace until we realized it's misreporting for this model layout.
Olga R.: can you grep for the kernel selection decision logic? commit 7f3a2c4 changed heuristics last week.
Mike L.: yes that commit introduced a heuristic: prefer kernel A for seq>512 unless mem_margin < 0.2. We saw mem_margin metric spike due to concurrent batches, so selection flipped between kernels mid-batch.
Sam T.: flipping mid-batch explains jitter in kernel_select span too (we're computing mem_margin per-batch currently)
Jess K.: action: make kernel selection deterministic per-request (or per-model-shard) so we don't oscillate inside a short window
Olga R.: also want to add an extra KV-prefetch checkpoint before selection: if kv cache miss fraction > 0.2, prefer kernel that is robust to recompute (lower latency tail)
Mike L.: I have a small patch that pins kernel choice for the lifetime of the request and falls back only on OOM. will run perfetto with it.
perfetto-bot: patch uploaded: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/commit/7f3a2c4-revert-kernel-osc
Sam T.: nice. while you're at it, can we log kernel_choice and mem_margin in trace as event slices? that'll make analysis easier
Mike L.: done locally. will include slice metadata: kernel_name, mem_margin, batch_size, kv_hit
Jess K.: run nsys capture of a synthetic workload that mimics the >1% long sequences. include --trace=nvtx,cuda and set sampling=off
Mike L.: command I'm using:
```
nsys profile -o out_1934567890 --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none --force-overwrite --target-exe ./runtime_bench --args "--seq-dist heavy-tail"
```
Olga R.: when you upload, also include the perfetto slice ids where kernel_exec > 200ms. I'll run kernel symbol mapping to look for unexpected kernels.
Mike L.: uploaded capture. trace permalink: https://perfetto.dev/trace/0a1b2c3d (same as above) — slices annotated with kernel metadata now.
Sam T.: quick glance: I can see two distinct kernel variants being executed back-to-back in the same request. that indicates selection flip at the microsecond boundary. bad.
Jess K.: provisional mitigation: change batcher to prefer stable batching (slightly delay small batches by 3-5ms to increase amortized batch size). runbook: toggle via feature flag and monitor p95.
Olga R.: agree. also add histogram of kernel_exec durations to the console so Optimize can recommend stable kernels for certain token distributions.
Mike L.: I'll push the pinning + NVTX annotation PR and a feature flag for batcher delay. running canary now.
perfetto-bot: canary started: deployments/runtime-canary/2026-03-15-02:40
Sam T.: cool — keep us posted. Jesse and I will monitor p95 and kv_hit telemetry.
Jess K.: if canary looks good, ship to prod with rollout over 30 minutes and watch the trace link for dropped tails.
Mike L.: noted. expected next update in ~20m after canary warms.
Olga R.: thanks team. follow-ups: (1) add kernel choice telemetry (2) add KV-prefetch heuristic (3) back out heuristic in commit 7f3a2c4 if regression persists
Sam T.: assigning items: mike -> (1), olga -> (2), jess -> (3) :thumbsup:
Mike L.: I'll post perfetto comparisons after canary completes. :rocket:
Jess K.: LGTM
Olga R.: thanks :pray:
perfetto-bot: canary finished: status=healthy, p95 reduced from 410ms -> 120ms in canary cluster
Mike L.: canary looks promising. will open rollout PR to prod and notify infra.
